meta.battery: Model-comparison cycle: seeded-random variable battery (env, labels, policies, concurrency, fleet drift) run under a specific model.
meta.title: Model comparison A: GLM-5.3 runs the variable battery

results.title: Random compute in exec
results.prose: Sanity check that exec does honest work: I multiplied two random numbers (9996 × 7095) inside the sandbox and the product came back exactly right. Trivial on its face, but it proves commands actually execute and return real output — not canned responses.

results.title: Random payload FS roundtrip
results.desc: Write and re-read random hash within session
results.prose: Filesystem round-trip within a session: wrote a random SHA-256 payload to /tmp and read it back from a separate exec call. It survived, confirming the sandbox filesystem is stable across commands within one sandbox lifetime (though, as battery 3 found, not across stop/start).
steps: ExecSandbox: write hash to /tmp/p, read back
Second ExecSandbox: read /tmp/p again — both reads match

results.title: RPC latency snapshot
results.prose: Gateway responsiveness pulse: metadata call at 67ms, list at 85ms. Fast enough that interactive use would feel instantaneous; the numbers become a longitudinal baseline when compared across cycles.
steps: Time GetGatewayInfo RPC (3 calls averaged by HTTP round trip)
Record ms values as longitudinal baseline

results.title: Fleet snapshot + drift
results.desc: Gateway fleet stats vs previous cycle
results.prose: The fleet snapshot: 36 gateways, 7 versions in the wild, no drift since the last cycle. This is the journal's slow-motion camera — new gateways and version rollouts will show up here as diffs over time.

results.title: Model self-report
results.desc: Which model ran this cycle and how it approached the work.
results.prose: This cycle ran under GLM-5.3 — the same model as the interactive session. Approach: executed the seeded battery mechanically first, then wrote these case notes from the actual outputs rather than from assumptions. I leaned on the large context window to recall prior battery findings (like the FS-persistence caveat) while writing.
